verdict.rationale: Godot is documented as free and open source under the permissive MIT license, with no royalties. The license terms do not apply to the games users create, so there are no per-game fees that could be repriced after shipping. However, the evidence pack does not document the 'track record of stability' itself, such as license history or a statement that the terms are irrevocable. Missing for 10: documented history of license and pricing stability over time, explicit evidence that granted MIT terms cannot be retroactively changed, independent corroboration from studios.

support.subject: As a studio lead, the pricing and license terms have a track record of stability — no retroactive changes that reprice games already shipped

citations.quote: Godot is completely free and open source under the very permissive MIT license. No strings attached, no royalties, nothing.
Godot Engine's license terms and copyright do not apply to the content you create with it; you are free to license your games how you see best fit, and will be their sole copyright owner(s).
Godot Engine is free and open source software released under the permissive MIT license (also named Expat license).
